paras: The killing of Robert Harvey was the killing of a Black man by Sheriff Lewis of Austin County, Texas, reported in a telegram from Brenham dated November 28, 1881. The telegram said Harvey was killed while resisting arrest and described him as "a cow thief and a bad negro." The two-sentence report ran in Waco and Dallas papers and is the only account found.

According to the Brenham telegram, Sheriff Lewis of Austin County killed Robert Harvey "while resisting arrest." The report does not say where or when the killing took place, how Harvey was killed, what warrant or charge the arrest was for, or whether anyone besides the sheriff was present. Its only explanation was the closing line, "He was a cow thief and a bad negro," a characterization attributed to no named source.
No report of an inquest, grand jury inquiry or other official review of the killing appears in the coverage.

The Waco Daily Examiner printed the item on November 29 as a "Special Telegram" under the heading "Closed by the Sheriff--Killed by a Sheriff," pairing it with news that a Brenham firm had been closed on an attachment. The Dallas Daily Herald ran the same two sentences, word for word, the same day as a "Special to the Herald" from Brenham, and the Dallas Weekly Herald reprinted them on December 1. In each printing the sheriff's version was given as fact, without attribution, and the dead man was identified chiefly by the labels "cow thief" and "bad negro."
No Black newspaper coverage of the killing was found, and no follow-up report from Austin County or Brenham was found.
